reason: Four-step unrolling tests a new loop schedule, but the prior two-step unroll was not promoted, so expected benefit is limited and unverified. The 288-byte scratch stride is distinct from the rejected 272-byte layout; cache benefit is unknown. Half-band packing is distinct from row-half-first traversal, but it adds packing work and changes traversal; the similar prior traversal was not promoted. The K-pair proposal may alias the measured two-step unroll and needs source-level distinction. The NEON transpose could reduce conversion cost, but the prior TB call lost badly and did not isolate conversion. TA adds a timed transpose while retaining generated B packing and adding A packing. Fused transpose recomputes each A element across 16 panels, making its expected cost and implementation risk highest. None has measured evidence of a gain.
